chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: Eclipse, The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady, and the Vanguard band
summary: Johnson asks about the Black Saint album; Mingus says a working band for three months let the music be played right.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yeah, I can appreciate that. Well, let me ask you about some specific things, then. You pointed out the writing on that particular little 45 as being something that I should hear, that you were very proud of. And I know the arrangement on "Eclipse." I think that's the same one that I worked on for the Philharmonic Hall concert, isn't it? Was that the record that you gave me?
I gave you the score to it, right?
Yeah. Yeah, that was beautiful. It sounds --
That was a long time ago.
Let me ask you then about pieces that I like of yours, I think are great. You wrote "The Black Saint and in the Sinner lady".
(inaudible) Yeah, I like that. it's more than alright --

And (inaudible) it's -- I know some of -- well, why don't you tell it? I know you had a band rehearsing at that time, and I wonder how much having a band available had to do with how much you were able to pull out of that band. You played at the Village Vanguard?
And why don't you say something about that?
Everyone should have a band to play with, and then they can get the music played right. That's
what was happening. We were there about three months, I think. Then I decided — (inaudible) I recorded it, to record it.
